item.title: JayQuery Accepted to the ACM SIGCSE TS 2027 Student Research Competition
item.description:
Work from our SCARP 2026 project, JayQuery, was accepted as a Student Research Competition paper at the ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE TS 2027).

The paper, “ Training Across FERPA Silos: A Differentially Private Vertical Federated System for Dropout Prediction” by Alexander Pellet, Wyatt Wilfong and Peilong Li, is scheduled in the ACM Student Research Competition session on Thursday, February 18, 2027 ( program). Congratulations, Alexander and Wyatt!

item.title: Dr. Li Presents ARISE at QRS 2026 in Florence, Italy
item.description:
From July 22-25, 2026, Dr. Li presented our paper “ ARISE: Adaptive Multimodal Orchestration for Real-time Conversational Health Agents on Heterogeneous Edge Platforms” by Peilong Li, Alexander Roop, Aaron Frist, Jingwen Wang and Juan Huertas at the 26th International Conference on Software Quality, Reliability, and Security (QRS 2026) in Florence, Italy. The paper comes out of our ARISE project (SCARP 2025).

At the conference, Dr. Li also served as the session chair for the Special Track on Dependable IoT and Edge Software Systems.

item.title: RydeeNLP at the ACM SIGCSE TS 2025 Student Research Competition
item.description: Yusuke Satani presented “ RydeeNLP: Personalized Japanese Learning Through NLP-Powered Proficiency Adaptation” at the Student Research Competition of the 56th ACM Technical Symposium on Computer Science Education (SIGCSE TS 2025) in Pittsburgh, PA. Congratulations, Yusuke!

item.title: MalBuster Paper Published at IEEE CCNC 2024
item.description: Our paper “ MalBuster: Scalable, Real-Time, and Concept Drift-Adaptive Malware Detection for Smart Environments” by Jingwen Wang, Peilong Li, Ethan Weitkamp, Yusuke Satani and Adam Omundsen appeared in the proceedings of the 2024 IEEE 21st Consumer Communications & Networking Conference (CCNC). Congratulations to our student co-authors!

item.title: MalIoT Preprint Released
item.description: Our paper “ MalIoT: Scalable and Real-time Malware Traffic Detection for IoT Networks” by Ethan Weitkamp, Yusuke Satani, Adam Omundsen, Jingwen Wang and Peilong Li is now available on arXiv.

item.title: Paper Published at NSysS 2020
item.description: Our paper “ Machine Learning Based Malware Detection on Encrypted Traffic: A Comprehensive Performance Study” appeared in the proceedings of the 7th International Conference on Networking, Systems and Security (NSysS 2020), held December 22-24, 2020. The paper is a product of our SCARP 2020 project. Congratulations to Matthew Grohotolski and Connor DiLeo, and thanks to our collaborators at UMass Lowell and Intel.

item.title: Paper Accepted by IEEE International Conference on Communications 2020
item.description:
ACETA Paper Accepted

Our paper entitled “ACETA: Accelerating Encrypted Traffic Analytics on Network Edge” was accepted to be appearing in proceedings of IEEE International Conference on Communications 2020. The average IEEE ICC paper acceptance rate is 38%. Congratulations to Derek Manning and the team.
